text:
eli: Heads-up — noticed a 6-8% token/throughput regression on the 1F1B runs after the kernel-selector change + new NCCL. Affects long-seq workloads (seq_len >= 2048).

maya: ugh. reproable on perf rig?

eli: yes, repro on cluster-pp-4gpu-stg. Quick trace shows all-reduce wall time up ~12% and throughput drop mostly during the last 2 microbatches in the bubble. KV hit-rate unchanged.

jonah: can you paste the perf snippet?

eli: sure:
```
# perf summary (avg over 10 runs)
step_time: 0.672 -> 0.716 (+6.5%)
allreduce_avg: 18.2ms -> 20.4ms (+12%)
compute_avg: 42.1ms -> 43.0ms (+2%)
microbatch_count: 8
1f1b_bubble_slots: 2
```

eli: also saw KV cache spill logs but only for 1 run out of 10, not correlated with bulk regression.

sam: did kernel-selector flip quantized GEMM or change algo for large seqlen?

eli: it toggles a different matmul kernel for >=1024 tokens to favor memory layout. That kernel has different prefetch+tiling.

jonah: NCCL upgrade notes mentioned progress-engine tweaks — could affect allreduce latency tail. Any NCCL traces?

eli: perfbot uploaded trace: /artifacts/pp/1835001234/nccl-trace.html (perfbot confirmed).

perfbot: @eli trace generated and uploaded: /artifacts/pp/1835001234/nccl-trace.html :white_check_mark:

maya: quick thought — if kernel increases compute slightly but changes timing alignment, we could be losing comm/compute overlap and making allreduce blocks fall into bubble end. Microbatch phasing is sensitive.

jonah: can you run a microbatch sweep? try microbatch 4/8/16 and also toggling the new kernel. compare end-to-end and per-stage timelines.

eli: started sweep on cluster-pp-4gpu-stg: running jobs with microbatch=[4,8,16], kernel_flag=[on,off], 3 runs each. Will post results in ~20m.

(18m later) eli: results snippet:
```
microbatch=4, kernel=on  -> step +3.2% vs baseline, allreduce +8%
microbatch=8, kernel=on  -> step +6.5% vs baseline, allreduce +12%
microbatch=16, kernel=on -> step +1.1% vs baseline, allreduce +3%
microbatch=8, kernel=off -> step +0.6% vs baseline, allreduce +1%
```

eli: interesting — larger microbatch (16) mostly recovers but increases memory pressure. kernel off also recovers but we lose the memory layout benefits.

maya: that suggests phasing shift — bigger microbatch increases compute window so allreduce can overlap better. When kernel on but microbatch small, allreduce sits on tail.

jonah: agree. Two angles: adjust batching heuristic to prefer larger microbatch when long seq or change kernel misaligned tiling parameters. Also could tune 1F1B schedule to insert a tiny prefetch pause to shift phasing.

sam: any KV cache effects? earlier you said occasional spills. Could eviction noise be contributing to tails?

eli: KV spill only on extreme memory runs (microbatch 16 borderline). For microbatch 8 we saw same regression w/o spills. So KV not primary culprit.

maya: action items:
- eli: open perf bug with full traces + step-level breakdown (attach nccl-trace, timeline flamegraphs).
- jonah: experiment with tiny 1F1B phase shift (insert 1ms scheduling jitter before last microbatch) and test on perf rig.
- sam: verify NCCL knobs (P2P, tree vs ring) and try downgrading communication plugin on one node to isolate.

eli: created bug: https://redwood/issue/PPBUB-517 (attached traces).

jonah: quick trial — added a 1.2ms sleep before finishing microbatch on stage 2 to nudge the allreduce into overlap. Result: restores ~4.5% of throughput on microbatch=8. Proof-of-concept only.

maya: nice. If we can tune heuristic to pick microbatch=16 on long-seq workloads by default (falling back to smaller microbatch when memory constrained) that's an easy win. 

eli: also logging note: kernel-selector should emit opt_reason tag (why chosen) and estimated phase_shift. Will add in PR.

sam: final thought — we should include per-stage NCCL latency percentiles in console dashboards so teams can see comm tail regressions quickly.

maya: agreed. I'll make a console ticket for UI metrics.

eli: thanks all. I'll keep the bug updated with microbatch sweep artifacts and a proposed heuristic change.

jonah: bravo. follow-up: if we can reproduce with a synthetic small-model faster, we can test kernel tilings faster.

maya: ping me once the PR for opt_reason is up and we'll roll a canary. :thumbsup:
